questions: Section 6 refers late-onset, well-controlled metabolic disease to judgement. For the 'late-onset' half: does type 2 diabetes diagnosed in 2019, when this applicant was about 49, count as late-onset under house practice, and if not, what age at diagnosis does?

For the 'well controlled' half of the same section 6 referral: does diet-only control with no medication and a current A1c of 6.7 count as well controlled under house practice, or does the house require an A1c below a particular level?
When the section 6 late-onset, well-controlled referral does apply to a file, what is done to the A1c debit: is it charged as the table reads, reduced to a lower band, or waived?

Section 16 refers combinations of cardiac risk factors to judgement. For a 56-year-old male with type 2 diabetes, HDL 37 (total cholesterol 170, ratio 4.6) and an untreated diastolic of 85, does the house treat that as a combination that adds a charge beyond what the individual tables give, and if so what is done?
